name: adv_sac_clean
title: Soft Actor-Critic, correct - three optimizers stepping in one block
note: A correct off-policy actor-critic. It carries no `expected` row and must carry no finding. Its value is the interleaving: `critic_opt.step()` at line 147 stands above `actor_loss.backward()` at line 155 in the same function body, which is the statement order MLV203 looks for, and the two are not linked - the file exists to prove that nothing fires on it. MLView measures 48 nodes / 42 edges and emits two coverage diagnostics (gymnasium has no knowledge table; `actor_loss` could not be typed), which is the honest answer rather than a clean bill of health.

forbidden.why: critic_opt.step() (147) precedes actor_loss.backward() (155), but they belong to two different updates with two different optimizers and two different losses; the critic's own order is zero_grad (145) -> backward (146) -> step (147) and the actor's is zero_grad (154) -> backward (155) -> step (156)
every one of the three updates calls zero_grad(set_to_none=True) before its backward: lines 145, 154 and 162
every backward is followed by its own optimizer step: lines 147, 156 and 164
the only no_grad blocks are soft_update (line 125), the target computation (line 137), the evaluation rollout (line 174) and the action selection (line 222); no backward() is inside any of them
update() returns three floats through .item() at line 167; nothing accumulates a live tensor anywhere
evaluate() calls actor.eval() at line 172 and actor.train() at line 187
evaluate() wraps its whole rollout in `with torch.no_grad():` at line 174
there is no cross-entropy of any kind in this project
there is no binary cross-entropy in this project
every tensor is built with device=DEVICE and the replay buffer allocates on the same device
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 36
seed_everything() at line 39 seeds random, numpy, torch and torch.cuda, and the replay sampler takes an explicit torch.Generator seeded at line 194
there is no train/test split call in this project; the replay sampler takes generator=
both nn.Module subclasses call super().__init__() on their first line (lines 50 and 80)
the two Q networks are held in nn.ModuleList at line 81
torch.save at line 239 writes a dict of state_dicts, not the modules
